$comment: Release manifest for candidate-4 (06-13-PLAN.md Task 2, 06-CONTEXT.md D-12/D-13).
Every value here is copied from a real continuous-integration run at the revision below.
Nothing in this file is measured locally. Where a lane has only local evidence, it is
recorded as BLOCKED with its reason, never as PASSED, because NOTHING LOCAL MAY BIND TO
LOCALLY BUILT BYTES (tooling/release-lanes.json).
WHY THIS CANDIDATE EXISTS AT ALL, stated plainly because a candidate cut hours after the
one before it deserves a reason. candidate-3 is bound to c2e4ce3 and left
weekly-historical-pitr BLOCKED, correctly: that fixture had passed, but at a different
revision, and a pass nearby is not a pass here. `workflow_dispatch` takes a branch, not a
commit, so once main moved past c2e4ce3 the drill could never be dispatched there again.
This revision is where all four workflow runs could be made to land together.
THE PRODUCT CODE HERE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO CANDIDATE-3'S. The three intervening commits
touch only .planning/ and KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md. That is measured, not asserted: the
package manifest's inputDigestSha256 is 713dd01d... at BOTH revisions. So this candidate
is not a claim that anything got better; it is the same software with its evidence
gathered at one revision instead of spread across two.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW HERE, and it is one lane:
* weekly-historical-pitr PASSES for the first time in any manifest, dispatched at this
revision as run 34780506996, its evidence naming this revision in its own file.
* All four drill fixtures except quarterly-host-replacement now pass at ONE revision.
* 23 of 39 lanes PASS, against 22 at candidate-3, 14 at candidate-2, 11 at candidate-1.
WHAT THIS CANDIDATE DOES NOT CLAIM:
* The passing drills say NOTHING about the backup credentials they demand or about any
real object store. The credentials gate a restore that never reads them. That is
.planning/WINDOWS.md row 100, it applies to daily-restore AND weekly-historical-pitr,
and it is the difference between 'the restore logic works' and 'we can restore'.
* desktop-e2e reports 66 passing tests of which ONE passed only on retry. Across four
runs of byte-identical code the flaky counts are 3, 1, 0, 1, and
guarded-navigation.spec.ts:135 appears in three of them. Row 101 records that this is
NONDETERMINISM and explicitly corrects candidate-3's stronger 'regression' wording.
* The build is still not reproducible, and this candidate is the cleanest demonstration
of it the project has: identical inputDigestSha256, different applicationDigestSha256.
* 16 lanes are BLOCKED and each says why, with an owner.
This manifest is EXPECTED to verify non-zero. A non-zero verdict carrying stated reasons
is the honest outcome at this revision; a pass would require a release claim this
revision's evidence does not support.
Verify with:  node tooling/verify-release.mjs --manifest .planning/releases/candidate-4/release-manifest.json
Offline with: the same command plus --offline (degrades only the attestation step).
READ THE ATTESTATION LINE CAREFULLY. verify-release.mjs reports attestation=UNVERIFIED for
every artefact entry here, online and offline. That is NOT a statement that no attestation
exists -- one does, it verifies, and its decoded statement is retained under
evidence/attestation/. It is a statement that the committed entries are RECORDS of the
released bytes rather than the bytes, and the attestation is over the bytes. Closing that
gap is .planning/WINDOWS.md row 96.

READ THE COUNT CAREFULLY. Playwright reports `Running 66 tests`, then `1 flaky` and `65 passed (2.5m)`: 65 passed first time, 1 passed only on retry, 66 passed in total. cases=66 is the number of passing tests; it is NOT 66 clean passes. THE FLAKY TEST IS test/e2e/guarded-navigation.spec.ts:135 (keyboard-initiated Discard Changes discards and completes navigation, matching the mouse-initiated outcome). THIS IS THE FOURTH SAMPLE OF ONE PROGRAM and the numbers are worth having together, because the e2e suite is byte-identical across all four: c2e4ce3 3 flaky (guarded-navigation:78, guarded-navigation:135, lifecycle:214), 12dbe9b 1 flaky (guarded-navigation:135), 9a0b062 0 flaky, 069df06 1 flaky (guarded-navigation:135). That test appears in 3 of 4 runs and is the only one to repeat, which makes it the single highest-value target. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: a regression. Candidate-3's manifest called it one against candidate-2's single clean run, and .planning/WINDOWS.md row 101 CORRECTS that -- a run reaching 0 flaky on the same code establishes nondeterminism, not a step change in it. The underlying defect is unchanged: all four of these runs are GREEN, and only the summary distinguishes a retried pass from a clean one. Row 101 is open and owned.

lanes.reason: Two independent things block this lane, and provisioning the credentials fixed neither. FIRST, the job body hardcodes `result: NON_PASSING` and `exit 1` before it reads any token, so it cannot pass whatever secrets exist; it has no runtime provisioning and materialises none of the five credential FILES the lane needs. SECOND, tooling/verify-host-replacement.sh requires eight inputs, five of them files outside the repository, and two of those inputs are not yet decided at all -- the DNS record name for the app host, and an SSH public key item. HCLOUD_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN are provisioned in the recovery-live environment (which had to be created; it did not exist), so the credential half is genuinely started, but the workflow half is untouched. THIS IS NOW THE ONLY DRILL FIXTURE THAT DOES NOT PASS AT THIS REVISION: run 34793473769 and run 34780506996 between them carry the other three, and this job was SKIPPED in both. DATA-03 and OPS-02 stay unchecked, which is the honest outcome. See .planning/WINDOWS.md row 95 as amended.

Unwired, by a deliberate open decision recorded as .planning/WINDOWS.md row 82: a notarized Developer ID build is not byte-reproducible by construction, so the lane needs a defined comparison that excludes the signature and staple before it can mean anything. THIS CANDIDATE MAKES THE POINT CONCRETE rather than theoretical: the package manifest's inputDigestSha256 is IDENTICAL to candidate-3's (713dd01d...), because the tracked inputs did not change between the two revisions, and the applicationDigestSha256 is nevertheless DIFFERENT. Two builds of the same inputs, two digests. That is exactly the comparison this lane would have to define away, and it is now measured rather than predicted.

Protected outer lane. Commit 1195bdc replaced the hardcoded deferral in tooling/test-phase-2.sh with a check of all nine required inputs: with every input present the lane now actually invokes tooling/verify-host-replacement.sh, and with any input absent it defers and NAMES the absent ones. Tested at eight of nine inputs, it still defers. So the lane is no longer structurally incapable of running -- but it still has no committed job that supplies those inputs (see quarterly-host-replacement above), so it has not run, and it reports BLOCKED with a zero case count. It provisions a real paid host and real DNS and is single-attempt; it keeps exiting non-zero so that no skip is ever counted as evidence.
